newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The National Bureau of Investigation in Western Mindanao is keeping a tight watch on all possible exit points in the region to prevent fugitive congressman Romeo Jalosjos from slipping out of the country. (ALL NEWSPAERS)

- The bicameral Congress committee resumes discussions in an effort to reach a compromise over an impasse between the Senate and the House of Representatives on the proposed 1997 budget. (BULLETIN/STAR)
- President Ramos ordered the implementation of salary increases for some 1.4 million government workers effective January 1 this year. (BULLETIN/STAR)

- Any failure by the government to fully implement three crucial structural reforms within the next six months may derail the country's much-awaited exit from the tutelage of the International Monetary Fund. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Central Bank is optimistic that the inflation rate will average at about 8.34 percent for the whole of 1996. (INQUIRER)
- PCI Leasing & Finance Corp lists today 121.22 million shares at 6.95 pesos apiece, the first initial public offering at the exchange this year. (TIMES)
- The Philippine government has accepted the US Trade Representative Office's offer to augment the country's garment exports quota by $40 million. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The government expects a 7.8 billion-peso budget surplus for 1996, 9.7 billion pesos short of the full-year target of 17.5 billion pesos. (BusinessWorld)
